items.title: Stale response suppression contract is explicit

items.title: Sync ordering, coalescing, rebase, and save semantics are explicit at policy level

dimension_assessments.summary: The seven units state their principal behaviors and negative constraints explicitly.
Document authority, message flow, stale suppression, identity mapping, synchronization, configuration, and timing controls are all represented as capabilities.
Identity and response inputs plus didSave and UI-output constraints are named, but comparator, normalization, encoding-failure, and consumer payload semantics are incomplete.
Strong high-level contracts exist, but key executable rules for conflicts, freshness, canonicalization, synchronization, and configuration remain unspecified.
Ready gating, stale discard, replacement or restart, pending sync, and failed-save effects are present, but the full transition and recovery state machines are open.
The single document authority is explicit, while conflict precedence and atomicity within that authority are not.
The LSP-specific owner document, retained external SSOT boundaries, and planning-only scope are explicit.
Document panes, editor tabs, chat virtual documents, and UI surfaces are named, but consumer API and lifecycle contracts are absent.
The core fixes UI dispatch and forbids stale or false-saved presentation, but leaves visible status, recovery, timeout, and settings interaction truth open.
Stale discard, failed-save suppression, whole-document replacement, and restart are present, but dispatch failure, backoff, replay, and recovery completion semantics are missing.
Environment values and project overrides are in scope, but no security, privacy, trust, secret, or redaction behavior is specified in the core.
Document and UI propagation routes are identified, but configuration propagation and consumer delivery guarantees are undefined.
Trace visibility, timeout controls, and session restart exist, but health, restart policy, retention, telemetry, and recovery oracles are not defined.
Nonblocking UI, FIFO sync, coalescing, and timeouts provide qualitative constraints but no measurable capacity or overload bounds.
The legacy alias and canonical destination are explicit, but conflict precedence, normalization, persistence, and retirement are not.
Plan migration and index validation are named, but no executable runtime oracle covers the seven LSP contracts.
Consequential discretion remains across conflict ordering, async lifecycle, freshness, URI normalization, synchronization, configuration, security, operations, scale, consumer APIs, and GUI states.
The high-level direction is clear, but multiple algorithmic, lifecycle, security, recovery, and presentation details remain ambiguous or unknown.
